Record the predictions of an automatic pre-pass without reviewing them

Source: R/batch_landmarks.R
accept_batch_landmarks.Rd

Writes the landmarks found by batch_landmarks() to the measurement journal as they are, without anyone looking at them – what the digitizer would record if every pre-filled photograph were saved untouched. It is meant for a large batch on which the model is known to do well; the price is that every error the model made is now a measurement.

Usage

accept_batch_landmarks(
  batch,
  journal_dir,
  operator,
  photos = NULL,
  include_flagged = FALSE,
  ruler_mm = 10,
  xlsx_path = NULL,
  dry_run = FALSE
)

Arguments

batch

Output folder of batch_landmarks(), or its returned list.

journal_dir

Folder of the landmark journal.

operator

Operator recorded with the records (who ACCEPTED them).

photos

Optional: restrict to these photographs (paths, file names or codes, i.e. file names without extension).

include_flagged

Also accept the photographs the pre-pass flagged.

ruler_mm

Real distance between landmarks 20 and 21, in mm, used for mm_per_px when the ruler was detected.

xlsx_path

Optional workbook rebuilt from the journal afterwards (consolidate_landmarks()).

dry_run

Report what would be recorded, write nothing.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame: photo, code, flags, status ("accepted", "dry-run", "flagged", "already measured", "plate", "no landmarks", "incomplete"), n_points.

Details

What is accepted, and what is not:

  • photographs the pre-pass FLAGGED (flags non-empty: upside down, at the border, low confidence, no readable ruler, several fish...) are left out unless include_flagged = TRUE – they are the ones a person should open;

  • a photograph that already has a measurement in the journal is never overwritten;

  • plates (several fish on one photograph) are left out, as in the digitizer;

  • the conventions of the digitizer are applied (perpendicular depths, derived ventral points and LM23), exactly as when a pre-filled photograph opens.

Nothing is hidden: every point keeps the status "predicted" (the derived ones "derived"), the entry is reviewed = "no", and the record says it came from here (app_version). landmark_journal_qc() and the Results of the hub list such specimens as not reviewed, and opening one in the digitizer (mode "correct") and saving it turns it into an ordinary, checked measurement.

See also

batch_landmarks(), digitize_landmarks(), retract_landmarks()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- batch_landmarks("prepared/T26/20260615", out_dir = "batch_T26")
accept_batch_landmarks(res, "measurements/landmark_journal", operator = "AT",
                       dry_run = TRUE)
} # }
